# C++ toolchain guides

What every compiler release supports, standard by standard, and what cpp-anything's generated code may therefore use. The data is cppreference's compiler-support tables; the recommendation is computed from it, not written by hand.

Refresh the data with `cpp-anything matrix sync` (or `scripts/sync_matrix.py`), then 
re-render with `cpp-anything matrix docs`.

## First release with complete support

Computed as the highest first-release among that standard's features: a release appears here only when it has every core feature (or every library feature) the matrix records. Features cppreference still marks partial do not block this number — each compiler's guide lists them, and `partial` is what `matrix features` reports.

| standard | GCC core | libstdc++ | Clang core | libc++ | MSVC core | MSVC STL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c++17 | 7 | 12.1 | 6 | — | 19.14 | 19.32 |
| c++20 | 12 | 14 | — | — | 19.31 | 19.42 |
| c++23 | 16 | — | — | — | — | — |

`—` means no release in the matrix implements all of it yet (or cppreference records no complete release). Partial support is common in both columns; see each compiler's guide for the gaps.

## How cpp-anything uses the matrix

- `bridge` writes `include/cppan/profile.hpp` for the chosen toolchain: one `CPPAN_HAS_*` macro per facility, computed from the matrix, plus a `static_assert` on the standard.
- Generated code uses `std::expected` (C++23). If the target cannot provide it, `gate` fails at the matrix step with the release you need, before a compiler error.
- `cpp-anything matrix features --toolchain X --version Y --std Z` answers "can this toolchain build the port" without compiling anything.
